project.name: QuietWindows
project.summary: Quiet Windows down so your games get the whole PC: PowerShell scripts and a menu that hold background Windows work while you play and restore it after.

docs.title: Overview
docs.summary: Windows PowerShell scripts with a click-through menu that put background Windows work on hold while you play, then hand it all back.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.summary: Two front ends (menu and one-shot setup) driving one folder of PowerShell scripts that share three libraries.

docs.title: Code map
docs.summary: Where every script, page and test lives, and where to look to change something.

docs.title: CPU detection
docs.summary: Works out which AMD X3D chip (if any) the PC has, where its big cache is, and which cores are safe for interrupts; never guesses.

docs.title: Extras (per-game fixes)
docs.summary: Drop a folder into extras/ and each .ps1 in it becomes a button on the Extras page; iRacing ships as the first one.

docs.title: Games list (My Games)
docs.summary: One saved list of the games on this PC, found from store folders or added by hand, used for Defender exclusions and stutter hunting.

docs.title: Checks and diagnostics
docs.summary: Read-only tools that say whether setup took, whether you are quieted, what reverted, timer behaviour, and CPU undervolt stability.

docs.title: Interrupt steering (GPU, NIC and USB)
docs.summary: Moves graphics-card, network and USB interrupts off the game's cores using the Windows interrupt-affinity policy; reversible.

docs.title: The dashboard (QuietWindows-Menu)
docs.summary: A WPF window of plain-language buttons that runs every script in its own window, elevated only when needed.

docs.title: One-time setup (the green button and Optimize-My-PC)
docs.summary: Applies the lasting fixes once (Defender exclusions, USB and Game Bar, task log, smooth timer, GPU interrupts), then asks for a restart.

docs.title: Quiet session (Start-Quiet and Stop-Quiet)
docs.summary: Puts Windows Update, Search, Store updates and background jobs on hold for a game, then puts everything back from a snapshot.

docs.title: Stutter finder (record, then find the cause)
docs.summary: Records what the PC does every second while you play, then names the program and often the file behind each stall.

docs.title: Operations
docs.summary: What you need, how to run it, how to run the tests, how a release is made, and the settings it reads.

docs.title: Interfaces
docs.summary: Every script's switches, the library functions other scripts call, the environment variables, and the files it writes for people.

docs.title: Data and state
docs.summary: The small JSON and text files QuietWindows keeps, where they live, and which Windows settings it changes.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.summary: The words QuietWindows uses for its own ideas, so code, docs and conversations mean the same thing.

docs.title: Known issues and open questions
docs.summary: Doc and code mismatches, limits, small debts, and the questions the code could not answer.

docs.title: ADR 0001: One shared quiet list in Kit-Common
docs.summary: The services and tasks to quiet are declared once, in Kit-Common.ps1, and every script reads that list.

docs.title: ADR 0002: Disable services and restore from a snapshot
docs.summary: Start-Quiet disables (not just stops) the quiet list and records the original state first; Stop-Quiet replays that record.

docs.title: ADR 0003: Fix scripts report their own failure
docs.summary: Every fix exits non-zero on a real failure and every elevation uses -ErrorAction Stop, so callers can tell success from failure.

docs.title: ADR 0004: Detect the CPU most reliable first, and never guess
docs.summary: CPU-Profile uses the name catalog, then cache layout, then cache size, then core count, validates against Windows, and skips X3D-only steps when unsure.

docs.title: ADR 0005: Menu layout in its own XAML file
docs.summary: The dashboard markup lives in ui/MainWindow.xaml instead of a here-string inside the menu script.

docs.title: ADR 0006: Pause Defender real-time scanning during a quiet session
docs.summary: Start-Quiet pauses Defender real-time protection for the session and Stop-Quiet turns it back on; -SkipDefender leaves it alone.

docs.title: Add an Extras folder for a game
docs.summary: Give one game its own buttons without editing any QuietWindows file.

docs.title: Add or remove a quieted service or task
docs.summary: Change what Start-Quiet turns off, in the one place that controls it.
